html:
A great temple in Palmyra, the caravan city of the Syrian desert, dedicated in 32 CE to Bel, chief god of the city, together with the moon god Aglibol and the sun god Yarhibol.

Palmyra grew rich on trade between the Roman world and the Parthian Empire, carried by camel caravans from the Euphrates. The temple shows that mix: Greek and Roman columns and decoration outside, but an inner shrine built for local rites, with altars on the roof. It stood in a vast walled courtyard. In the 200s Palmyra briefly built its own empire under Queen Zenobia before Rome crushed it.

The temple later served as a church and then a mosque, and a village lived inside its courtyard until the 1930s. In August 2015, during the Syrian civil war, the Islamic State group blew up the inner shrine; only its gateway was left standing. The same month its fighters murdered Khaled al-Asaad, the retired head of Palmyra's antiquities. The loss became a symbol of heritage destroyed in war.
sum: A great temple in Palmyra, the caravan city of the Syrian desert, dedicated in 32 CE to Bel, chief god of the city, together with the moon god Aglibol and the sun god Yarhibol.
